name: The Grafting Loom

detectability.signature: Tachyon string harmonics and cold dark-matter shear, strongest where filaments cross

proximity: Mass readings double, then halve, as if weighed on unseen scales
Gravitational ripples induce gentle structural groaning in hulls
contact: Threading a strand imparts sudden uncommanded acceleration
Navigation solutions smear across a dozen contradictory trajectories
prolonged_exposure: Hull breach from sustained tidal stress between crossing filaments
Permanent navigation drift requiring full system recalibration

behavior.cycle: Weave tightening and slackening on a roughly eleven-month cycle

phenomena: Unusual gravitational readings despite negligible luminous mass
Exotic particles detectable on sensors along the filament threads
Visible bending of starlight along the strands of the weave
hazards: Navigation system failure within the weave
Hull breach from gravitational stress at filament crossings
opportunities: Unique research opportunity for dark matter study
Hidden base location among the outer threads
known_incidents: Three freighters independently reported impossible acceleration near the same empty coordinates before the Loom was charted
description: A web of invisible mass spans nearly a full astronomical unit, betrayed only by the way starlight bends along its threads. Sensors read it as a lattice of tachyon strings and cold exotic particulate, densest where the strands cross. To enhanced optics it resembles a trellis of black vines woven across the void.

The Loom drifts through interstellar space at a steady crawl, dragging gravitational ripples behind it. Vessels passing between its strands report their mass readings doubling, then halving, as if weighed on unseen scales. Its weave tightens and slackens on a roughly eleven-month cycle.

Surveyors charted the structure after three freighters reported impossible acceleration near the same empty coordinates. Cartographers named it for the way its filaments appear to graft onto one another, joining and splitting like grafted stock. Research consortia now consider it the finest naturally occurring dark matter laboratory known.

The Loom remains open territory, though its core strands shift enough to make any route through it a gamble. Physicists continue arguing whether the weave predates the galaxy itself. Navigators are advised to skirt the outer threads rather than thread them.
